newsitem.title: FRANCE: No hard-and-fast plan for Cr Foncier - Arthuis.
newsitem.headline: No hard-and-fast plan for Cr Foncier - Arthuis.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Monday he had no hard-and-fast plan as far as the future of Credit Foncier de France was concerned.
"We must therefore build a plan with a future and discuss it with the partner or partners," he said.
Arthuis told a news conference only one partner, Credit Immobilier, had declared itself to date.
"We examine the proposals that are put to us," Arthuis said in defence of the government's stance.

The government has proposed spinning off part of the business of troubled home loans group Credit Foncier into Credit Immobilier and winding down the rest but ran into stiff resistance from staff, unions and some politicians.
The chairman of Credit Foncier declared himself a hostage on Monday and broke off talks with trade unions as a staff siege at the troubled bank's headquarters dragged into a fourth day.

Prime Minister Alain Juppe stepped into the dispute, naming former SNCF state railway head Philippe Rouvillois as mediator, calling for a return to business as usual and saying something had to be done because the state-controlled Credit Foncier was not viable.
